title: Targeted Practice — Relational Theory & PostgreSQL
description: Targets the owner's weakest ELO tags (database, postgres). Covers normalization, ACID/isolation, MVCC, and Postgres indexing. Uses all five question kinds.

questions.prompt: A relation already in 2NF reaches 3NF by removing which dependency?

options: Partial dependency on part of a composite key
Transitive dependency of a non-key attribute on the key

questions.explanation: 2NF already removes partial dependencies; 3NF additionally removes transitive dependencies (non-key -> non-key -> key).

questions.prompt: Unlike the SQL standard, PostgreSQL's REPEATABLE READ also prevents which phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Postgres implements REPEATABLE READ with snapshot isolation, so phantom reads are prevented too — the SQL standard permits them at this level.

questions.prompt: Which PostgreSQL index type best supports jsonb containment (@>) and full-text search?
questions.explanation: GIN (Generalized Inverted Index) indexes the elements inside composite values like jsonb, arrays, and tsvector.

questions.prompt: PostgreSQL's default transaction isolation level is Read Committed.
questions.explanation: Read Committed is the default; you opt into REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE explicitly.

questions.prompt: In PostgreSQL, VACUUM reclaims storage from dead tuples left behind by MVCC.
questions.explanation: MVCC keeps old row versions; VACUUM (and autovacuum) reclaims space and updates visibility/freeze info.

questions.prompt: In ACID, which property guarantees a committed transaction survives a crash?
questions.explanation: Durability — once committed, the effects persist even after power loss, typically via WAL.

questions.prompt: Write a SQL query returning the second-highest distinct salary from employees(salary).
questions.explanation: Subquery excludes the maximum, then takes the max of the rest. Graded manually against the exemplar (no code runner).

questions.prompt: Describe one situation where denormalizing a well-normalized schema is justified, and the trade-off you accept.

payload.rubric: Names a concrete read-heavy/reporting/latency scenario; acknowledges the cost (redundancy, update anomalies, write amplification).
